core_obligations: Set up the diagram: schemes $U, V$ with surjective \'etale maps to $X, Y$ and $U \to X \times_Y V$ surjective \'etale; reducedness of $X$ (resp. $Y$) is equivalent to reducedness of $U$ (resp. $V$) by definition (proof lines 1171-1182).
$U \to V$ is a smooth morphism of schemes (smooth-locality lemma); reducedness is smooth-local for schemes (cited Descent lemma), so $V$ reduced implies $U$ reduced (proof lines 1182-1188).
If $f$ is surjective then $U \to V$ is surjective, and a surjective morphism from a reduced scheme has reduced target in this setting, giving the converse (proof lines 1188-1192).
proof_roadmap: Lift to a scheme diagram over both spaces.
Transfer smoothness and use smooth-locality of reducedness for schemes.
difficulty_reason: The proof builds a diagram of schemes $U \to V$ over $X \to Y$ with surjective \'etale verticals and $U \to X \times_Y V$ surjective \'etale, transfers smoothness to $U \to V$ via the cited smooth-locality lemma, uses the definition of reducedness for algebraic spaces through charts, and applies the scheme-side smooth-topology locality of reducedness in both directions, plus surjectivity for the converse.
